BiblicalUsage: Bishlam means in peace, and he is named once, as one of the men who wrote against the rebuilding. In Ezra 4:7, in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam and Mithredath and Tabeel wrote a letter against Jerusalem, and the writing was in the Syrian tongue. A man named in peace, writing a letter of opposition.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bishlam's letter is the pattern of every opposition to God's work: it arrives in an official tongue, with official names, and it still fails.
